description.narrative: An initiative to mobilize African peoples across the continent to demand climate justice In Uganda , the caravan will mobilise youth and women from climate affected communities to rally inclusive COP27 Negotiations and demand for climate action at national, regional and global levels. Background: Across Africa, communities, countries, entire eco-systems are paying the price of global climate inaction. We are witnessing eco-system collapse at a scale never seen before and the depletion of natural resources – the soil, water and air humankind needs to survive – beyond the point of possible regeneration. But it doesn’t need to be this way. Uganda in Particular , climate change is causing unprecedented disasters that have resulted into colossal lossesand damages including loss of lives. In November 2022 COP27 will take place in Sharm-el-Sheikh, Egypt, and Oxfam will strive to ensure that political and financialcommitments are met to meet the high ambitions expressed in the last COP26 in Glasgow. Oxfam will push for a more inclusive and gender-transformative process in which action to respond to this existential threat happens when and where needed, which sees big emitters taking on their fair share of the burden by cutting emissions and helping payfor the climate response. This initiative will align with the objectives of the Oxfam advocacy strategy and contribute to the achievement of that, especially by ensuring that the voices of those most impacted by climate change are heard, through mobilizations, media, digital and financial support. The Caravan in Uganda is part of the Africa pre- cop27 caravan that will facilitate citizens’ participation in policy spaces at national, regional and global levels to show how women are leading their communities to become more resilient; where farmers are adapting their practices to protect food security and biodiversity; how indigenous groups are protecting eco-systems from collapse and how communities are finding ways to deal with the impacts of a crisis they are in no way responsible for. The people who are most impacted yet leastresponsible have something to say about it and governments across the world have a duty of care to listen and act. The Caravans toCOP27 will support these group in Ugandato be heard and push for action on adaptation and mitigation.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
